hints: Remember acid rain is not just any slightly acidic rain, it is caused by strong acids dissolving in rainwater.
Sulfuric acid comes from sulfur dioxide, so ask yourself which other non-metal oxide in the list can dissolve to form a second strong acid.
Think about what nitrogen dioxide forms when it reacts with water and oxygen, and whether carbon oxides or hydrocarbons can do the same.
walkthrough:
**Recall what acid rain really is**

Acid rain is rain with a pH well below 5.6 caused by dissolved strong acids. The question tells you one is sulfuric acid, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

The other main strong acid is nitric acid, $\text{HNO}_3$.

**Link each pollutant to its acid**

Sulfur dioxide is oxidised and dissolved to give sulfuric acid. In the same way, nitrogen oxides are oxidised and dissolved to give nitric acid:
$$4\text{NO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 4\text{HNO}_3$$

**Check the other pollutants**

Carbon monoxide is toxic but neutral and does not form an acid in water. Carbon dioxide only forms the weak acid $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$. Unburnt hydrocarbons lead to photochemical smog, not to strong acids. So only nitrogen dioxide fits.

options.A: Carbon monoxide, $\text{CO}$, is a toxic neutral gas. It binds to haemoglobin but does not dissolve in rain to form an acid, so it does not cause acid rain.
options.B: Carbon dioxide, $\text{CO}_2$, does dissolve to form weak carbonic acid, $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$. This makes natural rain slightly acidic (pH about 5.6) but it is not classed as the acid rain pollution problem caused by strong acids.
options.C: Nitrogen dioxide, $\text{NO}_2$, from high temperature combustion in car engines and power stations, is oxidised in air and dissolves in rain to form dilute nitric acid, $\text{HNO}_3$. This is the second major cause of acid rain alongside sulfuric acid.
options.D: Hydrocarbons are unburnt fuel molecules. They contribute to photochemical smog and ground level ozone, but they do not dissolve to give sulfuric or nitric acid in rain.
